label: prf:jucys-murphy-central-elements-qou
title: Proof of jucys murphy central elements qou
html:
Proof. Proof of jucys murphy central elements qou

Proof.

Step 1: JM elements commute. \sigma_{i,k} denotes the braid transposition swapping strands i,k in H_n(q). The relations

  J_k J_\ell = J_\ell J_k \quad \forall k, \ell

are a direct calculation from the braid relations of H_n(q); see Kassel (1995, §V.5) and Jucys (1974) for the q \to 1 origin (this works in \mathbb{C}[S_n]). The commuting subalgebra \mathbb{C}\langle J_1,\ldots,J_n\rangle \subset H_n(q) is the Gelfand–Tsetlin algebra.

Step 2: Symmetric polynomials in JM elements are central. Murphy (1992; the q-deformation of Murphy 1981) showed that the elementary symmetric polynomials P_\ell = e_\ell(J_1,\ldots,J_n) commute with every generator \sigma_i of H_n(q):

  \sigma_i P_\ell = P_\ell \sigma_i \quad \forall i, \ell.

The proof is by induction on \ell: P_1 = J_1 + \cdots + J_n = \sum_{i < k} q^{1-k}\sigma_{i,k} is centralised by every \sigma_j (each \sigma_j acts on the sum by permuting the transpositions, fixing the symmetric sum). The higher P_\ell are constructed from sums of products of J_k's; their \sigma_j-invariance follows from the same permutation argument applied at the level of multi-index summations.

Hence P_\ell \in Z(H_n(q)) for all 1 \leq \ell \leq n.

Step 3: Spectrum on Wedderburn blocks. The seminormal basis \{v_T\}_T (T = standard Young tableau of shape \lambda) diagonalises every J_k:

  J_k v_T = q^{2 c(\square_k(T))}\, v_T

where \square_k(T) is the cell of T containing k and c(\square) = j - i. (This is the Hoefsmit–Wenzl formula; see Kassel 1995 §VI.6 for the H_n(q) version.)

The seminormal basis decomposes V_\lambda as a direct sum over standard tableaux of shape \lambda. Symmetric polynomials in \{q^{2c(\square_k(T))} : k = 1, \ldots, n\} depend only on the multiset of contents — which is the multiset \{c(\square) : \square \in \lambda\}, independent of the particular tableau T. Hence

  P_\ell v_T =
  e_\ell\!\left(\{q^{2c(\square)} : \square \in \lambda\}\right)
  v_T

acts as the same scalar c_\ell(\lambda) on every v_T of shape \lambda.

By Schur's lemma (each V_\lambda is irreducible), this is the unique scalar action of the central element P_\ell on V_\lambda. \square

Corollary (closed form for level-\ell corrections). The level-\ell correction to the QOU mass formula is the \tau-extraction of P_\ell restricted to height-(\ell{+}1) partitions:

  T^{(\ell)}(\varrho)
  \;=\; m_e \cdot \frac{
    \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3A,\, \mathrm{ht}(\lambda) = \ell+1}
      w_\lambda(q) \cdot c_\ell(\lambda)
  }{[3A]_q!}

where w_\lambda(q) = \dim_q(\lambda)^2 / [n]_q! is the Wedderburn weight and \mathrm{ht}(\lambda) is the number of non-zero parts.

Application: \alpha_5 derivation. For \ell = 5, ht=6, this gives

  \alpha_5 \;=\; m_e \cdot \frac{
    \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3A,\, \mathrm{ht}(\lambda) = 6}
      w_\lambda(q) \cdot c_5(\lambda)
  }{[3A]_q!}

a finite combinatorial sum over height-6 partitions of 3A. This is the simplest closed-form ansatz consistent with the LP-dual characterisation of prop:mass-formula-iterative-lp-dual; it is conjectural, not implied by the central-element theorem.

Empirical status. The companion witness alpha-5-jucys-murphy-central.witness.json refutes this ansatz at \ell = 5: the relative spread of the normalised quantity across A \in \{2, 3, 4\} is \approx 482\% at q_0, and the spread is uniformly bad across the entire physical regime |q| \in (1, \varphi). The structural framework (Murphy 1992 + LP-dual extraction) is intact; the simplest closed form is not.
